A look at the gameplay concepts and build philosophy of Crimson Moon as a guide for XBOX players.
Forge Your Legend: Building the Ultimate Nephilim in Crimson Moon
When we set out to build Crimson Moon , we knew the combat had to feel extraordinary. Not just responsive – extraordinary. The kind of combat where every strike, every dodge, every perfectly timed Weapon Art feels like a deliberate expression of the warrior you’ve chosen to become.
That vision shaped everything about how Crimson Moon ‘s build system works. And with our September 1 launch on Xbox Series X|S just weeks away, we wanted to give the Xbox community a deeper look at one of our favorite things about the game: what it feels like to build your Nephilim from the ground up, hunt after hunt, until you’ve forged something truly legendary.
Gildenarch is a fallen city, but it is not an empty one. Its corrupted streets, graveyards, catacombs, and infected districts are crawling with hellspawn – and they carry extraordinary things.
Weapons and armor drop throughout every hunt, and the further you push into Gildenarch’s increasingly dangerous Wards, the rarer and more powerful the items you’ll find. A brutal run deep into enemy territory might reward you with a weapon you’ve never seen before, or an armor piece with statistics that completely change how you approach combat. That discovery – opening a chest in a place you’ve never reached before and finding something that makes you rethink your entire loadout – is one of the feelings we chased hardest during development.
The randomization is intentional. No two runs yield exactly the same rewards, and that unpredictability keeps every hunt worth taking seriously.
Everything you find in the field is temporary – until you make it permanent. When you return to Sanctus Clypeus, your home base between hunts, you can purify the items you’ve collected. Purified gear is yours to keep, regardless of what happens on your next run. The best piece of armor you found three Wards deep? Purify it and it becomes a permanent part of your arsenal.
From there, the real building begins.
Every Hunt is a Chance to Become Stronger

ledger.lastDecisionReason: 无AI兜底只收录窗口内、A级且具一手或两家独立来源的事实。

sources.label: PlayStation Blog
sources.evidenceText:
Michael Myers stalks heroes around lesser-explored parts of the iconic suburb.
Halloween: The Game – first look at the East Haddonfield map
Along with the music and iconic killer Michael Myers, the quiet suburban setting of 1970s Haddonfield is a pivotal element to capturing the legendary horror atmosphere and aesthetic of the Halloween franchise. As the design director for Halloween: The Game , it’s my job to help create the title’s technical and visual identity alongside my colleagues, and that challenge becomes a lot easier when you’re working within one of the greatest horror stories of all time.
While our game features recognizable locations and landmarks from the films, we also have an opportunity to showcase lesser-known parts of Haddonfield as we give killers and heroes different sandboxes for the multiplayer survival horror gameplay. One such area is our new map, East Haddonfield, and I’m excited to give PlayStation players a look into it for the very first time today.
Halloween: The Game’s other maps are primarily areas we’ve seen and explored throughout the movies. For East Haddonfield, we felt it was important to expand our vision of Haddonfield so that players could explore aspects of the setting that were only subtly touched on in the original 1978 film. We wanted to create spaces that fill in the gaps of the movie’s story.
East Haddonfield is a departure from the suburbs of the Midwestern town, going from residential houses to large industrial structures and small businesses flanked by farmlands, highways, and train tracks. It’s a more open, rural playspace centered around a huge grain mill, while also featuring silos, storage areas, and all sorts of nooks and crannies. 
The mill itself hosts several interior and exterior spaces that lead to unexpected confrontations and escapes. And in between the buildings, you’ll find wrap-around porches, farm equipment, dirt parking lots, and other signs that you’re on the outskirts of town.
This map also includes the neon-soaked Rabbit in Red Lounge and Phelps Garage, which should both look familiar to fans. All told, it’s a more chaotic version of the maps you find in the city: haphazard sight lines, uneven fence configurations, and buildings piled up and knotted together in ways that encourage strategic stealth and unique evasion tactics.

開発者のrentaka（れんたか）氏は9月1日、『 『スクジサマ』を巡る考察 』を発表した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）。発表に合わせて、動画やストアページなどが公開されている。
『『スクジサマ』を巡る考察』は、あるライターが遺したという資料などを読み解いていく、ホラーゲームである。本作の世界では、久我洋介というライターがある編集部に勤務していたようだ。久我はオカルト・民俗分野を中心に、取材や執筆などを実施。亡くなる数か月前から執筆は休止し、その後自宅にて遺体となって発見されたという。
本作『『スクジサマ』を巡る考察』は、ストアページを見る限りれんたか氏による新作のモキュメンタリーホラーとなるのだろう。同氏のX（旧Twitter）にて、ホラーゲームを開発していることや、謎の小物を制作している様子などが公開されてきた。本日Steamのストアページ公開とともに、タイトルも発表。概要なども明らかになっている。
『『スクジサマ』を巡る考察』は、PC（ Steam ）向けに開発中だ。
そこで“編集部”は、可能な限り発見当時の状態を維持したまま、資料を収録。久我によるデジタル作品を、株主への優待コンテンツとして、一般公開に先立ち配布するそうだ。なお編集部は、公開前に内容の確認をしているものの、収録データが膨大であり、性質上すべてを精査するには至っていないという。編集部には、久我洋介から本作について説明を受けた編集者はおらず、制作期間や完成時期も不明。どの段階まで制作していたのかもわからないそうだ。

The team reportedly worked 60 to 80 hour weeks to get the project out the door.
The majority of Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations was reportedly made under heavy crunch in just a few months.
This is according to an interview from Insider Gaming published yesterday. Andrew Willis, former producer at developer Id Software, spoke about the overtime involved in getting the DLC out of the door.
"There were two months where I was working something like at least 12 hours every day," Willis tells Insider Gaming. "I know I hit 17 a couple of days. It was brutal, and the majority of the game got made in three or four months."
The producer continues on to say that there were multiple instances in which more things continued to be added to the game, leading to more development time requirements. According to Willis, the number of hours depended on the week, but he recalls having reached "at least 80 hours" a few times.
"There were days where I didn't see my son the whole day; multiple days of that that I sacrificed to get this out the door at the level of quality," Willis says. "And it's not just me, but everybody on the team was really putting in the hours. We had people that worked in Hollywood for 20 years and game development for 10 and said that this was the worst crunch they'd been a part of."
Regarding the decision to work overtime, Willis refers to it as a "blurry line," explaining that it wasn't an official company mandate. Yet, since the work needed to be completed, it felt like that's what had to be done to finish the project.

'Did You Destroy My Favorite Game?': How the Heroes of Might and Magic 3 Community Is Guiding Ubisoft’s Reboot
"We really want to do right by them," says dev.
Ubisoft just revealed a remake of 1999's Heroes of Might and Magic 3 at Gamescom, and one look at the trailer shows it goes far beyond a simple polish and port. Set to release in 2027 across console and PC, the new game will swap the original's isometric 2D view with a 3D world and add new content - a fresh prologue campaign and some fancy cinematics - and tweak the original mechanics to make the game more accessible, without diluting the gameplay.
IGN spoke to Jean-Felix Monin, Creative Director at Ubisoft China, about the project and how the still very dedicated Heroes of Might and Magic 3 fanbase has been a key part of shaping this new version.
"I would say for us, the intention behind this game was really, there's this community, there's this great game that people have been kind of asking for a remake of for years now, and so we really want to do right by them," he said.
"We had contact with some key people in the community, people that we had worked with on other transmedia stuff, such as the board game, people that we knew we trusted and were quite representative and well-known, and they came and did some consulting."
This helped the team navigate some of the big changes, like the huge change from 2D isometric to 3D, complete with dynamic weather and seasons, and served as a north star for any gameplay changes. "So, the goal for us was to be really clear on the gameplay first. The gameplay is considered a masterpiece. And it's true that when you play the game, you really realize that, oh, wow, it's magical," said Monin.
"We took the decision really early on to not touch the gameplay. So, all the systems, all the balancing, had to stay exactly the same. We thought that through that, that would actually also address the question of, 'Okay, did you destroy my favorite game?'" he explained.

《黎明行者之血》是由Rebel Wolves工作室开发的一款单人第三人称奇幻动作RPG游戏。游戏背景设定在14世纪中世纪欧洲的“桑戈拉谷”，这里瘟疫横行、社会动荡，吸血鬼伺机而动。玩家将扮演名为科恩的“黎明行者”，在30个游戏日内拯救家人。白天玩家使用常规武器战斗，夜晚则可施展吸血鬼能力。游戏采用虚幻5引擎开发，画面精美，昼夜场景差异大。其独特的“血饥”机制和丰富的剧情选择，使玩家能获得沉浸式体验。
《黎明行者之血》是Rebel Wolves一次出色的首秀，也清晰标志着一个系列的开始。它充满了巧妙的设计理念，具备成为又一经典RPG系列的潜质。糟糕的性能表现和核心时间机制在一定程度上拖累了游戏，但我仍然会把它推荐给《巫师》的死忠粉和吸血鬼题材爱好者。
但从整体来看，《黎明行者之血》远不止这些。这是一款敢于做出不同尝试的RPG，而它的许多尝试也确实行之有效。体现在细微之处——比如铁匠可以将你的旧装备升级到与新装备相匹配的水平——在这些细节中，我能感受到Rebel Wolves的RPG专业功底与经验，感受到他们对RPG玩法如何能更上一层楼的理解。而这种理解，又以更大的尺度体现在游戏的结构设计和基础玩法逻辑之中。在主角科恩身上，Rebel Wolves发掘出了一个拥有双重面向的英雄，带来了美妙而令人欣喜的变化。在一个有时间限制且看似缺乏结构的世界中（尽管它并不像表面看起来那么无结构），他们找到了一种方式，让人们更关注自己所做的每一件事，更真切地沉浸在自己的冒险之中。我还不确定所有元素是否已经达到了完美的和谐共鸣，但这让我对这家工作室的未来充满了极大的期待。《黎明行者之血》是一部了不起的处女作。

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve’s multiplayer is built around three things: co-op and versus missions, customizing your aircraft, and the online lobby, which can accommodate up to 100 players at once. Ace Combat 8 is clearly aiming high.
Ace Combat 8's Multiplayer Is Aiming to Climb Higher Than Ever | IGN Preview
It’s hot in Germany. Most buildings don’t have air conditioning. Gamescom does, but it’s still hot and noisy, even in the business area that’s not as crowded. I’m here to talk about Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve’s multiplayer with Ace Combat Series Brand Director Kazutoki Kono and Ace Combat 8 Producer Manabu Shimomoto. I don’t get to play it myself, but I do get to see what they’re working on. And it looks impressive.
Wings of Theve’s multiplayer is built around three things: co-op and versus missions, customizing your aircraft, and the online lobby, which can accommodate up to 100 players at once. Ace Combat 8 is clearly aiming high. Shimomoto told me there were two reasons:
“First, while many customers enjoyed Ace Combat 7 and became fans, we received feedback from the community asking for a place where those fans could connect and interact with one another. In response to that feedback, we added the lobby to serve as a gathering place for fans. Second, thanks to everyone’s support, Ace Combat 7 is still selling well even seven years after its release. We designed it to be enjoyable for a wide variety of players—whether they prefer cooperative play or competitive play.”
Ace Combat 8 looks to have no shortage of either. Wings of Theve’s multiplayer is split into several mission types: Main Missions, which are always available and have rewards that scale based on rank; Emergency Mission, which are special, time-limited jaunts; and Event Missions, which are regular, time-limited missions with units to planes and roles.
It’s a lot, so let’s break it down. Each category is divided into two gametypes. For Main Missions, that’s Co-op Assault, where two teams of four compete for the highest score. Co-op Warfare is what really caught my eye, though. It’s a PvPvE mode where two teams of four (you’re gonna hear this phrase a lot, so bear with me) compete amid air, sea, and land units. Strategy will be based around what the team calls “Threat Level” and “Aces.”
When I asked about it, Shimomoto told me a lot of effort had gone into getting it right. “Co-op Warfare was created to address some issues in the series,” he said. “Up until now, Ace Combat’s multiplayer has had two problems: First, when players of similar skill levels face off, the two aircraft tend to circle around each other, fighting for position from behind, which makes it hard for the action to develop. We wanted to fix that. [Secondly,] we wanted to create a mode where aircraft other than fighters could also play an active role. In PvPvE, in addition to player enemies, NPC enemies also appear. It incorporates the “farming” concept from MOBA games, where defeating enemies raises the Threat Level. Especially early in a match, it’s easy to raise the Threat Level by defeating NPC enemies. For example, Attackers excel at raising the Threat Level by destroying large numbers of NPC aircraft, while Fighters excel at shooting down enemy players whose Threat Level has risen. We’ve succeeded in creating thrilling battles where a variety of roles shine.”
I never thought I’d hear Ace Combat compared to a MOBA, but if the Wings of Theve team has found a way to make sure that every playstyle can contribute and every plane has a role, Co-op Warfare is something I’ll definitely be keen to check out.

CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski opened up about the developer’s reaction to the rising price of consoles and the possibility of next-generation hardware getting delayed.
CD Projekt Red Boss 'Isn't Worried' About Delays for Next-Gen Consoles as RAM Prices Soar
CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski opened up about the developer’s reaction to the rising price of consoles and the possibility of next-generation hardware getting delayed due to RAMaggedon.
Speaking with The Game Business in a September 1 interview, Nowakowski said he’s “not worried” about console costs potentially affecting sales of CDPR’s titles.
“Consoles are still necessary to broaden the audience on the casual or semi-casual level. It’s important to have [something] easy to plug in and enjoy gaming,” he told the outlet. “I'm a big believer that they’re going to weather the storm. Pricing is the objective challenge. And the rumors... we hear them about the next gen being delayed. I don’t know if they’re true.”
He’s not very fussed about this possibility, either. For him, how CDPR reaches gamers is “a little irrelevant” — it’s the content that matters most, regardless of how it gets in players’ hands.
“Content is the king. And if the content is right, people will find a way to play it,” Nowakowski explained. “When we launch, if PS5, Xbox Series X/S is what people are playing, we’re going to be there. We’re going to find a business model that’s going to work for us, that’s going to be fine for players, and that’s it.
“If you ask the dev team, they will always answer: ‘Give us as much power as you can, because we want to show off the best stuff.’ That’s the way they’re wired. But they’re realistic. If the next-gen gets delayed, it could be the case that some ideas are put on a shelf for the future. We’d have to adjust. We’re not worried on the commercial side. Consoles are here to stay.”
This last bit is what’s raising eyebrows among fans. With PlayStation making the sweeping decision to end production of physical game discs starting January 2028, many are worried that consoles will eventually go the way of the Dodo if other big brands like Xbox or, God forbid, Nintendo, follow suit.
"They're going to weather the storm."

packages.headline: Godzilla Dev Wants to Do More Remasters, But 'a Lot of Conversations' Need to Happen First

sources.label: IGN Games
sources.evidenceText:
Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is the only remaster Pipeworks can confirm for now, but "a lot of stuff is on the table," and there are "a lot of conversations to be had" in the future.
Godzilla Dev Wants to Do More Remasters, But 'a Lot of Conversations' Need to Happen First
The developer behind the November upgrade and the 2002 game it's based on opened up about the potential for more games in the series during an all-encompassing interview with IGN. With Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee officially coming back, the natural question we and everyone else had is: Will we be getting remasters for Godzilla: Save the Earth and Godzilla: Unleashed ?
According to senior designer Simon Strange, it's too soon to say, but that doesn't mean he isn't rooting for it to happen.
Strange said a Pipeworks engineer recently created a tool that allowed them to bring old assets out of their original Spigot engine and into Unreal, thus resulting in Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered. He confirmed the same technology could be used to create upgraded re-releases for the rest of the studio's arena fighter trilogy, too. Unfortunately, the studio hasn't signed any relevant contracts with publisher Atari just yet.
When Pipeworks launched its original Godzilla game for GameCube in 2002, the team only consisted of about "12 people in one room." The company has since ballooned to include around 300 people who are often spread across dozens of different projects at any given time. That includes more focused games like Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered, as well as titles it's served as co-developer on, like Marathon, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Concord, and Destiny 2.
Choosing how to allocate those resources isn't simple, and whether the demand for more Godzilla remasters is even there remains to be seen. Atari and Pipeworks have nothing to announce, even if Strange loves "the idea of bringing all that content back to the players." The one catch, though, is that if more remasters do come to be, it would take a little more than a new coat of paint to get Godzilla: Unleashed into shape.
"I would especially love – and I'm speaking a little out of turn here – but I would love to avenge the sort of mediocre release of Godzilla: Unleashed," Strange said. "There was a lot of trouble on that, and I had a conversation where we were like, 'Would we remaster every possible game?' I was like, 'Nobody wants a straightforward remaster of Godzilla: Unleashed because that game was busted in some ways.' So, if we wanted to revisit that content, I'd want to do it better."
"I mean, all that stuff is now technically possible."

packages.headline: Aggro Crab launches publishing label to splash that Peak cash

sources.label: Game Developer
sources.evidenceText:
The studio wants to support 'intense, stylized games with an attitude' - but isn't interested in 'generative AI slop.'
Aggro Crab launches publishing label to splash that Peak cash
Peak and Another Crab's Treasure developer Aggro Crab has launched a publishing label and is actively soliciting submissions from teams building video games that are, in its own words, "absolute gas."
Aggro Crab Presents will support projects that require $500,000 or less to launch within two years. The company said it wants to nurture "intense, stylized games with an attitude" but isn't locked into any specific genres.
Crucially, Aggro Crab head of publishing Corey Warning said the team has no interest in publishing titles that leverage "generative AI slop."
The new initiative has been made possible thanks to the success of social climber, Peak , which has topped 20 million players worldwide since launching in June 2025.
" Peak's success put us in a unique position. We weren't really interested in significantly growing the size of our team, but we were interested in growing our catalog," added Warning. "We like to be hands-on with the projects we're working with, we can offer some unique perspectives and feedback to games from our background as indie developers and our experience self-publishing. We've also grown a massive community over the years who trust our approach to how we make and promote our own games."
Aggro Crab will take full advantage of its social media reach and existing audience to promote its publishing slate. It emphasised that Aggro Crab Presents is operated by the same people responsible for developing, vibe-checking, and playtesting the studio's own titles. This isn't a spinoff, but rather an extension of Aggro Crab's existing responsibilities.
"We want game devs who work with us to know that the same care and attention is going into promoting their game as any title Aggro Crab develops," said the studio. "We also want to publish games that we, the developers at Aggro Crab, are personally passionate about! We believe that enthusiasm for a project shines through on all levels, and so when we sign a game, it’s because we wanna be those devs' biggest fans."
